The range of options reflects Broadway's continued commitment to multigenerational entertainment, from timeless Disney adaptations to contemporary biographical musicals. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera**—which began its record-breaking run decades earlier but saw renewed critical attention during this period—reminds audiences why Andrew Lloyd Webber's mega-musical remains an enduring spectacle despite its camp sensibilities.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater just before and during an unprecedented period of disruption. These five productions showcase the range of dramatic work that defined the season, from bold reimaginings of classics to powerful examinations of social justice.

Leading the group is a grittier reboot of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely appreciate its fresh approach to the beloved musical, though the production has its detractors. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** makes a powerful, long-overdue Broadway debut with a stellar revival of Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama. Critics praise how this production demonstrates the work's enduring relevance in examining racism within the military, earning it a 78/100 across 29 reviews.

The season also features **Grand Horizons**, a boulevard comedy about a divorcing elderly couple that critics find pleasant if familiar, elevated by performances from Jane Alexander and the ensemble. Laura Linney commands the stage in the solo adaptation **My Name is Lucy Barton**, delivering what critics agree is a luminous performance, even as opinions divide on the adaptation itself. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves the most polarizing entry, with critics split between those who praise its bold vision and those who find the concept misguided.

With an average score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 plays demonstrate both the enduring power of classic material and theater's capacity for reinvention. Explore the full reviews to discover which of these productions might resonate with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a watershed moment for American theater. That year marked not only the industry's return from pandemic shutdown but also a creative renaissance that pushed theatrical boundaries in unprecedented ways.

The standout achievement remains **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama that continues to mesmerize audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's extraordinary lip-sync performance to a recorded interview. Critics consistently describe it as one of the most innovative theatrical experiments in recent memory, earning the highest marks among 2021's offerings with an 86/100 average across 23 reviews.

The year also brought Broadway's historic reopening with **Pass Over**, Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's urgent drama that blends Beckettian absurdism with the Exodus narrative to examine Black survival in America. Equally significant is **The Lehman Trilogy**, which transforms 164 years of American capitalism into an epic three-hour theatrical event featuring just three actors.

Beyond these headliners, 2021 showcased remarkable range: verbatim documentary theater in **Is This a Room**, virtuosic solo performances in **Lackawanna Blues**, and bold reinventions of classics like **Company** and **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**. Even **The Phantom of the Opera**, still running after decades, reminds audiences why spectacle and melody remain essential theatrical ingredients.

With an average critical score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the class of 2021 demonstrates that Broadway's reopening wasn't merely a return to normalcy—it was a creative rebirth. Whether you're catching final performances or discovering these shows for the first time, these productions represent essential viewing for anyone seeking to understand contemporary American theater.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2022 stands out as a remarkable year that brought audiences an exceptional collection of new productions and revivals. Leading the pack is **Kimberly Akimbo**, the quirky musical about a teenage girl with a rare aging condition that critics celebrate as a near-perfect achievement, deftly balancing laugh-out-loud comedy with profound emotional resonance. Close behind, the stripped-down revival of **Into the Woods** serves as a fitting tribute to Stephen Sondheim, earning widespread acclaim for its stellar performances and fresh interpretation of the classic musical. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's Pulitzer Prize-winning meta-musical, continues to receive praise for its brazenly original and brutally honest exploration of identity and creativity.

The 2022 season proves particularly notable for its celebration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works, with five featured productions having earned the prestigious honor. From Suzan-Lori Parks' electrifying **Topdog/Underdog** revival to Tom Stoppard's deeply personal Holocaust meditation **Leopoldstadt**, these shows demonstrate Broadway's commitment to challenging, substantive theatrical experiences. The season also showcases remarkable range, encompassing everything from Mike Birbiglia's masterful solo storytelling to Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satirical sketches in **Ain't No Mo'**.

Whether you're catching these productions during their current runs or exploring recordings and revivals, this collection represents some of the finest theatrical work to grace Broadway stages in recent memory.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2023 continue to demonstrate the remarkable artistic vitality of that season, with productions averaging an impressive 82/100 critical score across our featured selections.

The standout achievement remains **Merrily We Roll Along**, Maria Friedman's acclaimed revival that finally unlocked the emotional power of Sondheim's formerly troubled musical. Critics consistently praise its resonant performances and directorial vision that transforms the show's backward-moving chronology into devastating theatrical experience. Close behind, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that franchise extensions can achieve genuine theatrical artistry, with its technically stunning production values and narrative depth winning over skeptics who expected mere fan service.

The season also showcased powerful dramatic works, particularly **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama that features Sarah Paulson leading an ensemble cast through a modern examination of inheritance—both material and moral. The critical consensus positions it as essential contemporary American theatre.

Other notable productions include the long-overdue revival of **Purlie Victorious**, which demonstrates how Ossie Davis's 1961 satire remains bracingly relevant, and Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond's acclaimed performances in **Parade**, a revival that resonates with urgent contemporary significance. Solo performances also distinguished the season, with Alex Edelman's **Just for Us** and Jodie Comer's Broadway debut in **Prima Facie** earning widespread critical praise.

From Pulitzer Prize winners like **Fat Ham** to full-scale productions like **Sweeney Todd** and the music-driven **Buena Vista Social Club**, the 2023 Broadway season offered exceptional range and quality. For theatergoers planning their New York visits, these productions represent some of the finest work to reach Broadway stages in recent years.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves into spring 2026, the shows that opened last year continue to demonstrate remarkable range and vitality. This month's top ten plays—averaging a strong 84/100 from critics—showcase everything from timeless American classics to bold new voices, proving that serious drama remains a vital force on the Great White Way.

Leading the pack is Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons**, which earns the highest marks at 91/100 for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. The Belgian director's stark approach to Arthur Miller's 1947 masterpiece strips away period decoration to reveal the play's devastating moral core, resulting in what critics describe as one of the most powerful productions of the season.

Close behind, **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** (90/100) proves that musical theater with heart can also qualify as essential drama, with critics celebrating this 20th-anniversary revival's perfect balance of humor and tenderness. Meanwhile, Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer Prize-winning **English** (82/100) brings contemporary urgency to the lineup with its smart, sensitive exploration of language and identity among Iranian immigrants.

The list also features ambitious new works like Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose** and Sarah Gancher's **Liberation**, alongside major revivals of **Ragtime** and family-friendly fare like **Paddington The Musical**. Even the unconventional **Dead Outlaw**—a darkly comic musical about a mummified outlaw's bizarre journey—finds critical appreciation for David Yazbek's rock score.

Whether you're drawn to classic American drama, innovative new writing, or reimagined musicals, this month's selections offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:

Leading the year's new plays is **Every Brilliant Thing**, which earns an impressive 81/100 from critics across 19 reviews. Daniel Radcliffe delivers what reviewers describe as a warm and charming performance in this interactive solo show that tackles depression through an unexpectedly uplifting lens. The production invites audience participation as it explores life's small joys—from ice cream to the sound of rain—creating a communal theatrical experience that resonates deeply with critics and audiences alike. Reviewers consistently praise Radcliffe's ability to balance the material's emotional weight with genuine moments of connection and hope.

The strong critical reception for this production reflects Broadway's continued interest in intimate, character-driven work that breaks the fourth wall and challenges traditional theatrical boundaries. Solo shows and smaller ensemble pieces continue to prove their viability on Broadway stages, offering alternatives to large-scale musicals and ensemble dramas.
